rows.observed strokes: The word has an opening low cup and almost flat joined run, then one narrow long descending f-loop, followed immediately by a separate raised terminal t. I see no separately formed o/r/m humps between that f and the raised terminal. The shorter written contraction unift is favored, but the flattened joins do not securely distinguish all omitted or compressed letters, so I retain uncertainty rather than expand to uniformt. Comparison with the same-page f in the preceding fblt/fermee line confirms the descending-loop form, not the full letter sequence.

Two levels of ink are visible: a baseline glyph has a long descending stem and an angular right-hand return, but additional diagonal/horizontal crossing strokes obscure its identifying loop or bowl. Above it is a separate uncancelled small glyph: an open initial cup, short rise, long low rightward run and short downturned ending. The upper replacement supports mu, as does its open shape beside the similarly compressed support symbol M0368; the cancelled original remains mu/rho because its central strokes are overdrawn.

After pour the glyph starts with a tall near-vertical stroke, descends to a low point, and has a narrow enclosed return on the left of that stem. A separate shoulder rises to the right and ends downward, leaving the upper-right space open. This is visibly the deep-return/right-shoulder construction also present after d in M0367, rather than the small flat form above the cancellation in M0365. Neither the open shoulder nor the lower loop securely discriminates a rapid mu from rho in this occurrence; both candidates are retained.

The differential d is separately recognizable by its small leftward oval and upright return. The following glyph descends in a long slanted stroke, rounds a low pointed turn, then climbs to a right-hand shoulder with a short falling end. There is no clearly closed upper bowl; its construction resembles M0366, although this lower return is wider and open. That visible sequence does not securely select mu over a rapidly written rho, so the candidate uncertainty stays.

Immediately before the equals sign in the bottom inserted support formula, the small glyph has a short initial descending-return stroke, one low angular rise, and a long low rightward exit. It is open across the upper side, with no rho bowl and no sustained hanging stem. The same-page small replacement above the crossed M0365 glyph provides a similarly open compressed mu form. The preceding supp strokes are separate and are not being counted as part of this glyph.
